record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.context_brief: Robust matchings; approximability of minimizing b
record.original_question: For Stable Roommates instances with incomplete lists, determine the approximation complexity of finding a (1, b)-supermatch, or more generally a robust stable matching, that minimizes the repair parameter b.

evidence.quote: Genc et al. [41] also provided two metaheuristics for finding a (1, b)-supermatch for a given sri instance that minimises the value of b, however, the approximability of this problem has not been studied theoretically.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Stable Roommates problem with incomplete preference lists (SRI), defined as follows. Let A be a set of agents. Each agent a ∈ A has a strict preference list ranking a subset of A \ {a} (the agents it finds acceptable); acceptability is symmetric. A matching M is a set of disjoint acceptable pairs. A pair {x, y} with x, y unmatched-to-each-other in M blocks M if x and y find each other acceptable and each of x, y is either unmatched in M or strictly prefers the other to its partner in M. A matching is stable if it admits no blocking pair.

Given a stable matching M and an integer b ≥ 0, M is called a (1, b)-supermatch if, for every agent a that is matched in M, after removing the pair containing a from M one can repair the matching by altering the assignments of at most b other matched agents so as to obtain another stable matching of the remaining instance in which a remains unmatched only if necessary (equivalently, after any single forced break-up, stability can be restored by modifying at most b additional pairs). More generally, define a robust stable matching to be one that can be repaired under any single perturbation by changing at most b pairs.

Problem: Determine the approximation complexity of the following optimization problem. Given an SRI instance that admits at least one stable matching, find a stable matching M and the smallest integer b such that M is a (1, b)-supermatch (or more generally, a robust stable matching with repair parameter b). Specifically, establish the best possible polynomial-time approximation ratio for minimizing b, and prove matching hardness-of-approximation lower bounds (assuming P ≠ NP or standard complexity hypotheses).
artifact.status_search_result: Existing work introduces (1,b)-supermatches for Stable Roommates and provides metaheuristic (local search and genetic) algorithms for minimizing b, along with a polynomial-time verifier via reduced rotation posets. Deciding existence of a (1,1)-supermatch is known to be NP-complete, but the approximability of minimizing b (approximation ratios, hardness of approximation) has not been resolved in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: An Approach to Robustness in the Stable Roommates Problem and its Comparison with the Stable Marriage Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Local search and genetic local search procedures to find a (1,b)-supermatch minimising b in SR instances; polynomial verifier via reduced rotation poset.
status_evidence.claim: Only metaheuristic approaches are given for minimizing b; theoretical approximability is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: A Minimax Perspective on Almost-Stable Matchings
status_evidence.snippet: Robustness notions for stable matching including (a,b)-supermatches are studied with complexity results.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work studies related robustness notions but the approximation complexity of (1,b)-supermatch minimization in SRI remains unsettled.
